subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core pace-aware provider usage controls for autonomous agents, and should the first step be observability-only or include enforcement?
rationale: Source inspection shows the behavior is missing, but implementing it would introduce provider-specific usage semantics, persisted pace state, new agent config, and autonomous throttling policy that require maintainer product direction.

options.title: Phase Observability First
options.body: Expose provider usage and pace context in status/session_status without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

options.title: Add Opt-In Enforcement Now
options.body: Introduce disabled-by-default pace thresholds that can throttle subagents, with explicit config, tests, and operator recovery guidance.

options.title: Defer To Plugin/API Design
options.body: Keep core lean and first design provider/agent hooks so a plugin can own pace policy without hardcoding Anthropic behavior in core.

recommendation.title: Phase Observability First
recommendation.body: Expose provider usage and pace context in status/session_status without blocking agent or subagent work until the data model proves reliable.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history match for provider usage/status/auth-profile behavior and was already identified in the durable ClawSweeper comment as the likely decision owner.
